text:
Lia: quick RFC follow-up — we've run into a few API/observer gaps when wiring the canary coordinator to runtime for automatic fallbacks. collecting notes + decisions here :spiral_notepad:
Samir: examples? what gaps exactly? :eyes:
Lia: two big ones: observer contract can't express soft-degrade vs hard-fail, and we lack a stable way to pin session affinity when we divert traffic mid-session. also some ambiguity in metric tags for rollback triggers.
Maria: +1. also saw that the current probe only returns boolean pass/fail; we need richer signal (latency percentiles, error class, quality score).
Devin: sounds like we need a tiny v2 for the runtime "observer" API. proposed fields: "degrade_mode" enum, "session_affinity_hint", and "quality_score" float.
Kevin: what are acceptable enum values? I suggest: FAIL_OPEN, FAIL_SILENT_DEGRADE, FAIL_CLOSED. Keep names explicit.
Samir: we should avoid "silent" wording, maybe SOFT_DEGRADE vs HARD_FAIL vs BLOCK. semantics: SOFT_DEGRADE = continue but route to cheaper variant + lower tokens, HARD_FAIL = fallback to previous model, BLOCK = return error to client.
Lia: agreed on wording: SOFT_DEGRADE / HARD_FAIL / BLOCK. we'll map to existing fallback policies.
Maria: also need TTL for affinity hints. if you cutover mid-session we want per-session TTL so we don't oscillate. default 5m?
Devin: 5m seems fine, make configurable per-rollout.
Kevin: for metrics tags: add "rollout_id", "variant", "probe_type", "quality_bucket". rollout_id must be stable across retries.
Samir: how do we communicate the preference to the proxy? header? config?
Lia: proposal: Coordinator sets X-Rw-Rollout: <rollout_id>; X-Rw-Preference: prefer:variant-a, fallback:variant-b; X-Rw-Affinity-TTL: 300
Devin: header semantics allow easiest rollout without touching existing wire protocol. proxy/runtime can read and bind session cookie.
Maria: we need to define a small JSON payload for the observer response for richer signal. e.g.:
```json
{
  "status": "SOFT_DEGRADE",
  "quality_score": 0.87,
  "latency_pXX": { "p50": 45, "p90": 120 },
  "tags": ["nlp:relevance", "source:canary-3"],
  "affinity_hint": "session-12345",
  "affinity_ttl_seconds": 300
}
```
Samir: love it. how do controllers act on quality_score? threshold config in rollout plan?
Lia: yes — rollout plan has fail_on_quality_below, degrade_on_quality_below, and min_sample_size. default degrade threshold 0.75, fail 0.6.
Kevin: what about transient spikes? windows + min_samples will help but also want short-circuit if latency > 500ms for p90.
Devin: add probe_type metric so ops can set different thresholds for latency vs correctness.
opsbot: alert: canary probe failing in staging for rollout r-2026-03-19 (p90 600ms) — see /ops/canary/r-2026-03-19 :warning:
Lia: thanks opsbot. we'll fold that into rollout rules.
Maria: need to update the eval harness to produce the quality_score and tags. that touches eng-ml. cc @Samir for score contract.
Samir: i'll draft a minimal scoring spec today.
Devin: implementation notes for runtime: observe endpoint should be idempotent and cheap. don't block serving on heavy evaluation. maybe streaming partial signals then final verdict.
Kevin: for rollback decision engine, we should have two modes: conservative (only HARD_FAIL triggers) and aggressive (SOFT_DEGRADE triggers rollback if persists). config per-customer.
Lia: action items:
- Samir: scoring spec + threshold examples (due EOD)
- Maria: update eval harness + CI check for quality_score (due Wed)
- Devin: observer v2 proto and header reader in proxy (PR by next week)
- Kevin: rollout plan schema update + docs (RFC follow-up)
- Ops: add probe alerts mapping to rollout policies (ops-oncall)
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-controller v0.23 -> staging (job 4921) :rocket:
Devin: i'll open a PR with the proto and sample header parsing snippet:
```go
type ObserveResponse struct {
  Status string `json:"status"`
  QualityScore float64 `json:"quality_score"`
  AffinityHint string `json:"affinity_hint"`
  AffinityTTL int `json:"affinity_ttl_seconds"`
}
```
Maria: quick nit — make quality_score optional, default -1 to mean N/A.
Samir: ack.
Lia: thanks all. trying to keep this light — if no objections i'll merge the schema PR after Samir's scoring spec. :thumbsup:
Kevin: +1
Maria: +1
Samir: +1
opsbot: note: runbook updated: if p90>500ms and quality_score<0.7 -> auto-degrade then notify #oncall :white_check_mark:
Lia: wrapping up — placing final decision in the rollout RFC doc. Will ping again for review.
